summary: The machine builds its kernel, its utilities and its shell from its own sources on a KRFFS root, and what it built runs

cases.behavior: The machine builds its own kernel on a KRFFS root with the staged TinyCC and pdpmake twice, to the same bytes, the host takes the bytes it built off the disk and checks them, and GRUB starts them to a login prompt and to the debug shell, where every probe of the default suite passes

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machines and removes the disk copies and the evidence, which it keeps after a failure

steps.does: read the free space of the root of a copy of the os-real disk on the host, with setidcheck from its free-node chain
boot the copy and wait for the console's login prompt
log in at the console as the test account with its password
copy /src/rach2 to a workspace, build the kernel with make -f guest.mk, and hash it and set it aside in /home/test
copy /src/rach2 again, build the kernel again and compare the two hashes in the guest
sync the root and end the machine with QMP's quit
take the kernel set aside off the copy with readfile.krffs, hash it with sha256 and check it with elfcheck
write the kernel in place of the placeholders in the candidate and recovery slots of a copy of the GRUB disk with mcopy, and read each back
boot the GRUB disk under SeaBIOS to the login prompt of os-simple's ext2 root, and end the machine
select the recovery entry in the menu file of the GRUB disk, boot it to the debug shell of the test image in RAM, run each probe of the list there and end the machine

assertions.checks: the root has the 24 MiB a build needs free before the machine starts
the test account logs in at the console and its shell prompts
make -f guest.mk in a copy of /src/rach2 exits 0
the kernel the build made is at least 200000 bytes
a second make -f guest.mk in a fresh copy of /src/rach2 exits 0
the two builds made kernels with the same SHA-256
the kernel taken off the disk has the SHA-256 the guest gave it
elfcheck --kernel --tcc accepts the kernel taken off the disk
the candidate and recovery slots of the GRUB disk read back as the kernel written there
GRUB starts the kernel the machine built to the login prompt of os-simple's ext2 root
the kernel the machine built prints its record of its clock's check at level 6 at boot
every probe of the default suite's PROBES table that the architecture builds exits 0 at the debug shell of the kernel the machine built, none killed by a signal
clockmusl prints CLOCKMUSL REFERENCE OK, its result of comparing the guest's clocks with the host's reference over UDP

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended
a build of the machine's own sources has ended
a probe has handed the debug shell back

timing.assumes: the guest's calendar clock moves by at least one second across the probe's sleep of two seconds

native.reason: the guest builds on a private copy of a disk root and the kernel it built boots from a GRUB disk that the scenario writes

cases.behavior: The machine builds its own utilities and shell on a KRFFS root with the staged TinyCC and pdpmake, and the programs it built run: the file tools, the network tools, the refusals of the credential tools and the shell

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machine and removes the disk copy and the evidence, which it keeps after a failure

steps.does: boot a copy of the os-real disk and wait for the console's login prompt
log in at the console as the test account with its password
copy /src/utils and /src/ish to a workspace and build each with make -f guest.mk
run the programs the machine built, each check a line of its own, and end the machine

assertions.checks: the test account logs in at the console and its shell prompts
make -f guest.mk in a copy of /src/utils exits 0
make -f guest.mk in a copy of /src/ish exits 0
the cat built copies a file to standard output
the echo built prints its argument
the true and false built exit 0 and 1
the pwd built names /tmp in /tmp
the ls built lists a file of /tmp
the touch and mkdir built make a file and a directory
the cp, mv and rm built copy, rename and remove a file
the yes built prints y
the ping built has an answer from 127.0.0.1
the httpd built, once it says it listens on port 8080, answers GET / with status 200 to the nc built
the build made halt, init-shell, init-login and adduser-crash
the login built, with no terminal input, refuses with status 1
the su built, with no password, refuses with status 1
the sudo built refuses the test account with status 1
the passwd built, with no input, refuses with status 1
the adduser built refuses the test account with status 1
the bootctl built refuses to install a kernel with status 1
the ish built runs a command given with -c
